newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks give up gains, end little changed.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks give up gains, end little changed.

text.p: Swiss shares closed little changed after a gradual decline in the second half of the session after a weaker Wall Street open.
Roche certificates also sagged, weighing on the market generally.
The market was somewhat disappointed with Friday's performance, a Swiss stock dealer said. One trader expected the market to continue consolidating in the next few days.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) added 0.5 points, or 0.01 percent, to end at 3,812.0 points.
The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) advanced 0.79 points, or 0.03 percent, to 2,439.66 points.
Roche certificates were pressured by foreign sales, yielding 45 francs to 9,710 francs.
Ciba added five francs to 1,603, while Sandoz was unchanged at 1,505.
Nestle soared seven francs to 1,410 francs, drawing strength from Unilever's good figures.

UBS bearer shares were up nearly one percent to 1,236. Traders said the shares were sought ahead of a press conference of German Viag on Monday. A Viag unit recently recently expressed interest in Swiss utilities and UBS has a majority stake in Swiss utility firm Motor-Columbus.
Second-tier Motor-Columbus jumped 1.5 percent to 2,700 francs.
SBC was still under pressure from Thursday's nine-month figures. The stock fell one franc to 248.50.
ABB were up three francs to 1,586. Dealers said some switches from Siemens into ABB may have helped the stock.
